It was released on January 10, 2020, and later confirmed to be the third single from the former's eighth studio album ''[[High Off Life]]''.<ref name="Album">{{cite web|url=https://www.rap-up.com/2020/05/12/future-announces-new-album-high-off-life/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200515051459/https://www.rap-up.com/2020/05/12/future-announces-new-album-high-off-life/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 15, 2020|title=FUTURE ANNOUNCES NEW ALBUM 'HIGH OFF LIFE'|work=[[Rap-Up (magazine)|Rap-Up]]|author=''Rap-Up'' Staff|date=May 12, 2020|access-date=May 12, 2020}}</ref>

It debuted and peaked at number two on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and became the first song ever to spend its first eight weeks at that position, behind [[Roddy Ricch]]'s "Life Is Good" is a song by American rapper Future featuring Canadian rapper Drake. It was released on January 10, 2020, and later confirmed to be the third single from the former's eighth studio album High Off Life.

It debuted and peaked at number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 and became the first song ever to spend its first eight weeks at that position, behind Roddy Ricch's "The Box". It was Future's highest-charting song as a lead artist and his highest-charting song overall, until  the releases of "Way 2 Sexy" (with Young Thug) and "Wait 4 U" (with Tems), two more collaborations between Future and Drake that both debuted at the top of the charts. The track sold 9 million units in the US by March 3, 2021. The song was certified diamond by the RIAA on November 22, 2021, for selling over 10 million units in the United States.

sections.heading: Background and music video
sections.wikitext:
In late December 2019, Future and Drake were spotted in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], filming a music video in a [[McDonald's]] location,<ref name=Complex>{{cite web|url= https://www.complex.com/music/2019/12/drake-future-spotted-in-mcdonalds-for-what-appears-to-be-music-video|title= Drake and Future Spotted in McDonald's Reportedly Shooting a Video |work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|last=Espinoza|first=Joshua|date=December 21, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref> leading to the belief that the two had a forthcoming collaboration. The shoot included recording artists such as [[21 Savage]], [[Mike Will Made It|Mike Will Made-It]], [[Lil Yachty]] and Big Bank Black. Word of the video spread when media personality [[DJ Akademiks]] posted the casting call for the video. Future had previously posted a snippet of what the duo were working on in his [[Instagram]] story.<ref name=Complex/>

The song and music video, directed by [[Director X|Julien Christian Lutz (Director X)]] were released at midnight on January 10. The music video depicts Future and Drake as men with ordinary jobs, including fast food workers, mechanics, IT workers, off-brand [[Apple Store]] employees, garbage men, chefs, aspiring rappers, and assistant directors. As of April 2025, the music video has amassed a total of 2.2 billion views on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nayvadius |first1=Cash |title=Future - Life is Good (Official Music Video) ft. Drake |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l0U7SxXHkPY |website=youtube.com |access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/10/entertainment/drake-future-life-good-trnd/index.html|title= Drake and Future debut 'Life is Good' video|work=[[CNN]]|last=Respers|first=Lisa|date=January 10, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.vulture.com/2020/01/watch-future-and-drake-hold-down-jobs-in-life-is-good-video.html|title= Future and Drake Are Just Normal, Working Joes in 'Life is Good' Video|work=[[Vulture (blog)|Vulture]]|last=Squires|first=Bethy|date=January 10, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref><ref name=MTV>{{cite web|url= https://www.mtv.com/news/3152082/drake-future-life-is-good-video/|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200110205459/http://www.mtv.com/news/3152082/drake-future-life-is-good-video/|url-status= dead|archive-date= January 10, 2020|title=Drake and Future Keep Losing Jobs Because They Can't Stop Dancing in 'Life Is Good'|work=[[MTV]]|last=Alston|first=Trey|date=January 10, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref>
sections.text:
In late December 2019, Future and Drake were spotted in Atlanta, Georgia, filming a music video in a McDonald's location, leading to the belief that the two had a forthcoming collaboration. The shoot included recording artists such as 21 Savage, Mike Will Made-It, Lil Yachty and Big Bank Black. Word of the video spread when media personality DJ Akademiks posted the casting call for the video. Future had previously posted a snippet of what the duo were working on in his Instagram story.

The song and music video, directed by Julien Christian Lutz (Director X) were released at midnight on January 10. The music video depicts Future and Drake as men with ordinary jobs, including fast food workers, mechanics, IT workers, off-brand Apple Store employees, garbage men, chefs, aspiring rappers, and assistant directors. As of April 2025, the music video has amassed a total of 2.2 billion views on YouTube.

sections.heading: Remix
sections.wikitext:
On February 15, 2020, a remix of the song was released by Future featuring Drake and American rappers [[DaBaby]] and [[Lil Baby]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Diep |first1=Eric|title=Listen to Future and Drake's "Life Is Good" Remix f/ DaBaby and Lil Baby|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2020/02/future-drake-new-song-life-is-good-remix-feat-dababy-lil-baby|access-date=February 15, 2020|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|publisher=Complex Media, Inc.|date=February 15, 2020}}</ref> Three days prior to the release, Future teased DaBaby and Lil Baby's vocals on an [[Instagram]] story. The remix is featured on Future's eighth studio album ''[[High Off Life]]'', along with the original version.

A remix of the song was released by [[Lil Wayne]] off his mixtape ''[[No Ceilings 3]]''.
sections.text:
On February 15, 2020, a remix of the song was released by Future featuring Drake and American rappers DaBaby and Lil Baby. Three days prior to the release, Future teased DaBaby and Lil Baby's vocals on an Instagram story. The remix is featured on Future's eighth studio album High Off Life, along with the original version.

A remix of the song was released by Lil Wayne off his mixtape No Ceilings 3.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext: Jason Lipshutz of ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' wrote that structuring the song in two halves—Drake performing the first half and Future performing the latter, each with a different beat—was reminiscent of Drake's previous feature on [[Travis Scott]]'s 2018 hit "[[Sicko Mode]]". The review praised how the artists' styles complemented each other as they did on their joint mixtape in 2015.<ref>{{cite magazine|url= https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/first-stream-nselena-gomez-future-drake-mac-miller-megan-thee-stallion-8547741/|title= First Stream: New Music From Selena Gomez, Future & Drake, Mac Miller & More|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|last=Lipshutz|first=Jason|date=January 10, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref> ''[[XXL (magazine)|XXL]]'' described the production and instrumentation as "dreamy chords with a mid-tempo vibe".<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.xxlmag.com/rap-music/new-music/2020/01/drake-future-life-is-good-song/|title= Drake and Future Drop New Song "Life Is Good": Listen|work=[[XXL (magazine)|XXL]]|last=Coleman II|first=C. Vernon|date=January 10, 2020|access-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref>
